text:
Sasha: Heads-up — after the routing policy tweak yesterday p99 latency for /v1/generate jumped ~2.5x for a subset of routes. Feels like the new priority routing is skewing tail quantiles. Anyone else seeing this?

Alex: seeing it in the dashboard too. p50 barely moved, p95 up ~20% and p99 spiking. Looks like a small number of requests are getting routed to the low-cost pool with longer cold-starts.

Maggie: can we confirm whether streaming responses are included? Those inflate tail if we measure end-to-end until EOF.

Dan: good call — our current PromQL uses histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)) which counts whole request time. Streaming finish time is counted.

Sasha: that's the issue then. For streamed endpoints we should measure "first-byte" latency for tail SLOs and separate end-to-end for correctness/time-to-complete.

Paul: +1. Also noticed sample size for some low-traffic routes is tiny, so p99 is noisy. Need to add sample_count alongside percentiles in the dashboard.

Maggie: I'll open a quick panel that shows count(rate) and tdigest quantiles (we have tdigest summary for more stable estimates). Example query I used locally: ```
# tdigest example (Influx/metrics-adapter)
quantile(0.99, tdigest_digest)
```

Alex: for Prometheus we could switch to summaries with objectives or use clickhouse/observability backend that supports TDigest. Important: document which estimator we use because comparing dashboards across consoles is confusing otherwise.

Sasha: Routing policy side — we recently added "spill_to_economy" when reserved capacity hits threshold. Those econ workers are docker-on-cpu-backed gpus with higher init latency. That policy is exactly what would send a few requests into a long-tail path.

Dan: can you post the rollout config? I want to see the thresholds. If we tweak the spill threshold up a bit, it might reduce tail impact but cost increases.

Sasha: config snippet: ```
route_policy:
  - name: default
    prefer: reserved
    spill_to: economy
    spill_threshold_qps: 1200
    spill_percent: 5
```

Paul: If the spill_percent is 5% we expect 1-in-20 requests to go to economy. With a fat-tailed service time distribution, those 5% can dominate p99. Maybe make spill deterministic by route weight rather than blind percent?

Maggie: UX/console note — dashboard should annotate when policy changes occur. Right now it looks like a regression but it's expected given routing change. Annotations + modeling overlay (expected p99 given new weight) would help support/PMs.

Alex: Agree. Also want per-endpoint breakdown by model + region + priority bucket. This would let us see if it's global or region-specific.

Sasha: For short-term fix: 1) exclude streaming EOF from p99 panel (use first_byte metric), 2) show request_count next to each percentile, 3) annotate routing-policy change event on chart.

Dan: long-term: move p99 calculation to a robust aggregator (tdigest) and compute per-route t-digest on the ingestion side so we can roll up safely across pods. Also add a smoothing window and a minimum-sample threshold before surfacing p99 as a SLA.

Paul: Also update alerts — current p99 alert fires when p99>500ms for any route. That will noise if count<50. Change to alert only when count>100 in 5m.

Maggie: I'll prototype dashboard changes and push a PR for the console annotations + sample_count. Sasha can you file a short RFC for changing spill logic? We should include cost tradeoff numbers.

Sasha: filing RFC now, will tag @alice for cost ops review.

monitoring-bot: New alert group created: "p99-spike-routes" — temporarily suppressed by on-call per Sasha's request.

Alex: Thanks. Quick checklist: update panels, add first_byte metric, show sample_count, annotate deployment/routing changes, adjust alert thresholds.

Sasha: perfect. If anyone wants to pair on the tdigest ingestion write me. Might need infra help to add the aggregator

Maggie: will follow up with a tiny mock dashboard by EOD. :rocket:
